notes.title: Director Letter #3
notes.notes:
Hello, everybody! I am Niizato, director of Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3.

Today I'm going to dive a bit deeper into a new battle system introduced in Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3—the weakness combo. Enemies in the Fuga: Melodies of Steel series have always had weakness icons, and you could delay enemy actions by destroying them. In Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3, repeatedly destroying these icons will result in a weakness combo which increases the base damage of your attacks.

[b]⚙️Weakness Combos[/b]
To start a weakness combo, you'll first need to get a Combo Chance by destroying an enemy's weakness icon. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/46df717c580e4ad8219f89cc50a968f4055f2449.png[/img]

Destroy another weakness icon afterwards to start a weakness combo and gain a damage multiplier for your attacks, including on the attack that started the combo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/356f2f3dcf78f964076a767899c0f2a59de620e7.png[/img]

Your damage will increase with your combo, allowing you to deal up to twice as much damage! Keeping your combo up will be the key to victory.


Here's a little tip as well: [u][b]you can use area of effect (AoE) attacks to help build your weakness combo.[/b][/u]

For a group of enemies with the same color weakness icon, using an AoE skill of the same color will destroy all those icons, raise your weakness combo by that amount, and deal more damage accordingly! What's more, the damage increase from raising your weakness combo is applied to the same hit that triggered it.

For example, if you are fighting three enemies with blue weakness icons (meaning they are weak to machine guns), then Mei's Multi-Piercing Shot will destroy all three of their weakness icons at once. This one attack would raise your weakness combo from 0 to 1 to 2 and your damage from 100% to 120% to 140%—which is then applied to that very same attack!

While AoE skills may be very handy, [u][b]they also cost a lot of SP to use![/b][/u] Keep an eye on your resources and be on the lookout for the perfect time to blast away!

notes.title: Director Letter #2
notes.notes:
Hello, everybody! This is Niizato, director of Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3.

Today I'd like to share with everyone the finer details of one of the new mechanics in Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3—the Akasha Panel.

The Fuga: Melodies of Steel series has always been about the choices you make. From the Soul Cannon to route selection, all the choices you make can lead to different endings.

This is especially true of Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3, where your decisions will not only dictate whether you get the Normal Ending or the True Ending, but [u][b]unlock different character events and Special Endings.[/b][/u] The Akasha Panel changes visually according to the choices you make, giving you a stress-free way to see the outcomes of your choices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/3d02f1e48876fa92599f65e4a23475c6aeaa79bf.jpg[/img]

Optional nodes can also be found alongside the chronologically ordered nodes on the Akasha Panel. These nodes can be unlocked and played, and today, I'd like to give you a closer look at one of them.

Assist Events
By raising your Bravery and Tactics levels with the new Assist System in Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3, you'll be able to recruit powerful assist characters to your party and call upon them to attack for you in battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/0f590d73c74c2845b8ea64bb2387064bf85ba436.png[/img]

Among the assist characters that can join you on your journey is a former enemy—Flam Kish. She faced off against the children as an enemy general, before facing a terrible defeat. Why is it that she has decided to now help her former foes? You can find out for yourself in the Akasha Panel!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/12e2a8cbc6225ca3adef7675b21a22cca460e46a.png[/img]

Unlock this episode of her past in the Akasha Panel by recruiting her to your party.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45456446/7483fb07e0202cc94ec9b8ea1536cd815aa6b9ff.png[/img]

Learn what happened to Flam after her defeat at the hands of the Taranis, and even more! The Akasha Panel will let you know all about a character's past, and even... their future!

notes.title: Director Letter #1
notes.notes:
Hello everybody! This is Niizato, the director of Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3.
Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3 will finally be releasing on May 29th, and in anticipation of that there are a few things I wanted to share.

[h3][b]Please, please play Fuga: Melodies of Steel 1 and Fuga: Melodies of Steel 2 first if you can![/b][/h3]
While we took the greatest care to make sure that Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3 could be enjoyed without having to play the previous games, it is the finale in the series, and [u][b]we're sure you will enjoy Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3 even more if you know about the characters as they appeared in previous titles, or about the story that is coming to a conclusion in this latest chapter![/b][/u]

[h3][b]Clear the game in a breeze with Fast Mode![/b][/h3]
[previewyoutube=4j83XTrLFxc;full][/previewyoutube]
The new update brings Fast Mode to Fuga: Melodies of Steel 1 and 2. Put very simply, [u][b]Fast Mode makes you invincible during battles.[/b][/u] The Soul Cannon of the Fuga series forces you to sacrifice a child to defeat an enemy, but Fast Mode has no demerits whatsoever, allowing you to quickly cut through your foes. What's more, [u][b]you can even use Fast Mode in the middle of your normal playthrough as a separate save data.[/b][/u]

This means that once you've played through to the end and had your fill of the story with Fast Mode, you can go back to your original save point and enjoy the game again, this time with the battles in place. But of course, how you choose to enjoy the game is entirely up to you! Please treat it simply as an option that exists for your benefit.

You can choose to enter Fast Mode from the very start of Fuga: Melodies of Steel 3, but as someone who has worked on the game I can't personally recommend doing so. My suggestion is that you first play through the newly powered-up battle system, and if you need to, you can always change to Fast Mode halfway through!

notes.title: Announcing Patch 1.50 Update for Fuga: Melodies of Steel
notes.notes:
■Patch Notes (Version 1.50)
・Turbo Mode/Auto Text status can now be saved. 
・Improved visibility when enabling/disabling Turbo Mode/Auto Text.
・Turbo Mode is now available to players starting from their first playthrough—and its speed has been doubled.
・Retry Mode has been added to help players who missed the true ending.
・Corrected the colors of HP/SP waypoints to match the color of the gauges.
・Changed default key assignments of confirm/cancel for keyboard control.
・Added a feature to check the status of the Taranis from the item trade screen.
・Increased the battle tempo.
・The newly added binoculars lets you check the enemy's status right from the formation screen.
・Improved usability of the formation screen.
・Improved visual effect in the battle result screen.
・Cross-key control is now supported during intermissions.
・Improved usability of character change UI for intermissions.
・Improved visual effect of unlocking facilities.
・Added the automatic harvesting of crops before each intermission.
・Improved usability of Farming UI.
・Improved usability of Dormitory UI.
・Improved usability of Laundry Room UI.
・Improved usability of Observation Room/Expedition UI.
・Default page of the status screen is changed to a character in control.
・Improved visibility of the item trade menu.
・Other improvements include: Operational stability and bug fixes

We hope this helps improve your Fuga: Melodies of Steel gameplay experience.

notes.title: Fuga: Melodies Of Steel is a strategy RPG with a giant child-powered tank
notes.notes:
Fuga: Melodies Of Steel is set during an anthropomorphic animal anime World War 2 in which your parents have been taken by the dog Nazis. Still with me? You and your fellow cat children find Howl's Moving Tank in a cave and set about getting your families back, with turn-based, RPG battles.

You also discover at the end of the tutorial that your giant angry house has a "Soul Cannon", which is a gun that only fires if you feed it the soul - and permanently kill - one of the children.
